UAE Semiconductor Workers Walk Out, Halting Chip Production Across Major Sites

DUBAI, June 21 — Thousands of workers in the United Arab Emirates’ semiconductor industry staged a walkout on Friday, disrupting production at several key fabrication sites and assembly plants across the country, company officials and union representatives said.

Employees from at least four major firms, including Gulf Silicon Systems, Emirates MicroFab, and Advanced Chips UAE, stopped work at midnight after negotiations over pay and working conditions broke down late Thursday. It is the largest coordinated industrial action in the country’s semiconductor sector to date.

Production lines at Gulf Silicon Systems’ Sharjah facility, one of the region’s leading producers of logic chips, have come to a complete halt, according to company spokesperson Fadi Al-Hamidi. “We have activated contingency protocols, but wafer processing and assembly operations are currently suspended,” Al-Hamidi said.

At Emirates MicroFab’s Abu Dhabi campus, a notice was posted at entrances early Friday informing staff that “all cleanroom operations remain paused until further notice.” A company official, speaking on condition of anonymity, said the facility was running at less than 10% capacity, with only essential maintenance teams present.

The UAE Semiconductor Workers Union, which represents an estimated 7,500 employees, said the walkout was called after months of stalled negotiations over wage increases, shift schedules, and safety standards. “We have exhausted all options,” said union chairperson Marwan Al-Ketbi. “Our members are proud of their contribution to the country’s high-tech ambitions, but they deserve fair compensation and safe working conditions.”

Industry analysts say the immediate impact has been a shutdown of wafer fabrication, testing, and packaging operations at multiple sites. “The UAE has positioned itself as a regional semiconductor hub, so any sustained disruption will have significant implications for output and delivery timelines,” said Fatima Al-Mansoori, a semiconductor market analyst based in Dubai.

The walkout has left an estimated 10,000 workers off the job, according to the UAE Semiconductor Industry Council. “We urge all parties to return to the negotiating table without delay,” said council president Omar Nasser in a statement, warning that “extended downtime places our industry’s reputation and future growth at risk.”

As of Friday evening, talks between union leaders and company representatives had not resumed. Workers gathered outside facility gates in Sharjah, Dubai, and Abu Dhabi, holding signs calling for “fair pay for vital work.” There have been no reports of violence or arrests.

Officials from the Ministry of Industry said they are “closely monitoring the situation” but declined to comment on ongoing discussions. The strike is ongoing at the time of writing.
